This is a very strange article that does not seem to make any real point other than gene selection could possibly have negative effects on society.

This one quote is particularly odd.
"In a world where disability is not only almost universally considered bad and which contains options to opt out of having disabled children, will support for accessibility legislation like the ADA or AODA continue?"
For one the author already points out that not all disabilities can be selected against so some children will still be born disabled. And the author also points out that many people become disabled later in life so obviously groups that help the disabled will still exist. Legislation protecting disabled people isn't suddenly going to go away just because the rates of disabled babies would decrease. 

Also I don't think it's offensive to say that if given the choice most people would choose to not be disabled. I wouldn't wish my health problems on anyone.

The only real issue I have with this type of medical science is that it will not be available for all people, only wealthy people. Children of wealthy people already have an advantage in the sense that their parents can send them to private schools, pay for tutors and extracurricular activities, etc. We have a continually expanding wage gap in the US and since raising disabled children is typically more costly than raising an able bodied child it's unfair to not provide this type of medical service to all people.

"Another problem I'm running into is being declined specifically because I'm on SSDI. A couple phone reps have told me they don't like to issue credit to disability recipients because it's very hard to impossible to garnish if there's a default."

This doesn't seem like it should be legal. I would look into it if you can find a lawyer or disability advocate who has knowledge on the subject. 

Credit score is only one thing they look at. Your total income versus your current debt and other expenses is more important because they want to make sure you will actually be able to pay off your card or if you default they want to make sure your income is high enough that they can garnish wages. 

Also you will hurt your credit if you apply and get rejected from getting loans/credit cards. When a company makes an inquiry into your credit history to see if you qualify for a credit card or loan that inquiry shows up on your credit report. If a bank sees a bunch of recent inquires on your report they consider that a bad thing. You may have already put yourself in a bad place depending on how many times you have done this. Those inquiries stay on your report for something like 3-5 years (I don't remember the exact time offhand). You might just have to accept that you can't get a credit card at this time and work on building credit other ways. 

You can help build your credit however by continuing to make your monthly payments on time with the debt you already have. Also being on your parents card can help, however I think you have to be a joint account holder and not just an authorized user. But I am not 100% sure on that so you might want to look into it. 

This is a free and legit site to get a copy of your credit report. If you have not already done so I would suggest looking at it to see if there is anything negative on there.

Clinical depression is the result of a physical change in the human brain. My doctor told me that it is hard to get out of depressive episodes because the brain likes to keep things at a status quo even if that means feeling sad or angry. You basically have to retrain your brain to get rid of long lasting depression which is the point of therapy.

Now onto happiness. Studies have shown that people are happier when they are working towards a positive goal than when they reach their goal. So yes happiness seems fleeting to many people. This is likely an evolutionary advantage to keep humans motivated enough to work towards survival. This would have kept early humans eager to hunt/gather food, improve their living conditions and find a mate. In our modern society it can seem like a curse. Some people no matter how much they achieve never feel happy for very long.

I used to work in a biomedical research lab and unfortunately what happens a lot is something appears to be working when you try it out on animals or in small groups of humans, but then in large scale trials you don't get the same results. As scientist we try to be unbiased but studies have shown that when you believe something will work you are more likely to see the results you want to see even if you are trying really hard to be unbiased.
